title: Quillen B: a comma category models the homotopy fiber
statement:
Use small categories, ordinary nerves, geometric realization, Kan complexes and homotopy fibers as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Write $R(K)=\operatorname{Sing}(|K|)$, where $\operatorname{Sing}(T)_n=\operatorname{Cont}(|\Delta^n|,T)$ with precomposition operators; use the natural characteristic-map unit $K\to R(K)$. Let $U:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a functor between small categories. For each $b$, let $(U\downarrow b)$ have objects $(e,\alpha:Ue\to b)$ and arrows $h:e\to e'$ satisfying $\alpha'U(h)=\alpha$. Suppose every $\beta:b_0\to b_1$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence $N(U\downarrow b_0)\to N(U\downarrow b_1)$ by postcomposition. Then the canonical map
$$c_{U,b}:R N(U\downarrow b)\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{b}(RNU)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. The vertex $b$ on the right is the constant singular simplex at the nerve vertex $b$. The map is induced by the forgetful functor $(U\downarrow b)\to\mathcal E$ and the natural transformation from its composite with $U$ to the constant functor at $b$: realize this transformation, apply $\operatorname{Sing}$, and restrict the singular interval along $\Delta^1\to\operatorname{Sing}([0,1])$. Here the homotopy fiber uses the path-space model of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The comparison is natural for strictly commuting squares $GU=U'F$ of functors and specified objects $b\in\mathcal B$, $b'=G(b)\in\mathcal B'$: the comma functor is $(e,\alpha)\mapsto(F(e),G(\alpha))$, and the homotopy-fiber map is induced by $RNF$ and $RNG$. Both functors $U,U'$ in this naturality assertion satisfy the stated comma-transition hypothesis. No assumption that the comma categories are contractible is made.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.12, printed p. 183 (PDF p. 198), applied to opposite categories; its overcategory form, followed by contraction of B/b to its terminal object, gives the comma homotopy-fiber comparison. Read online on 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text: Put $D_b=(U\downarrow b)$. Define a bisimplicial set $Z_{m,n}=\coprod_{b_0\to\cdots\to b_m}N_nD_{b_0}$. A simplex is equivalently a pair of chains $e_0\to\cdots\to e_n$, $b_0\to\cdots\to b_m$, and an arrow $\alpha:Ue_n\to b_0$. The $m$-faces compose/delete base arrows, applying postcomposition to $\alpha$ when deleting $b_0$; the $n$-faces are comma-nerve faces, composing $\alpha$ with $U(e_{n-1}\to e_n)$ when deleting $e_n$. Identities give degeneracies. Functoriality of composition verifies all simplicial identities and commutation of the two directions. Write $Y_m$ for the discrete simplicial set of base $m$-chains; $\operatorname{diag}Y=N\mathcal B$. The projection $Z_m\to Y_m$ and the augmentation $t:\operatorname{diag}Z\to N\mathcal E$ forget respectively the $e$-data and the $b$-data.

proof.text: For each base chain replace its comma nerve by $RN D_{b_0}$, giving $X_m=\coprod_{b_0\to\cdots\to b_m}RN D_{b_0}$ and $p_m:X_m\to Y_m$. Every singular realization is Kan: by the realization--singular adjunction a horn map is a continuous map from the realized horn, and the realized horn-pair retraction extends it over the simplex. A horn in a coproduct lies in one summand (also in dimension one), so $X_m$ is Kan and $p_m$ is a Kan fibration to its discrete base. The characteristic-map units give a rowwise weak equivalence $Z_m\to X_m$ by [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak]. Naturality of those units also shows that $R$ preserves weak equivalences, by cancellation of component bijections and homotopy-group isomorphisms. Thus [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] makes $d:\operatorname{diag}Z\to\operatorname{diag}X$ a weak equivalence over $N\mathcal B$. Choose a single larger universe containing all singular-simplex sets.

proof.text: For an operator $a:[l]\to[m]$, the induced map over a base chain restricts on its fiber to $RN D_{b_0}\to RN D_{b_{a(0)}}$, given by the composite base arrow $b_0\to b_{a(0)}$. This is a weak equivalence by the comma-transition hypothesis and Step 2. All structure squares of $p:X\to Y$ are homotopy pullbacks: the strict pullback has a summand $RN D_{b_{a(0)}}$ over each original $m$-chain and its comparison from $X_m$ is the just-verified weak equivalence on each summand. Its path-space pullback is exactly that strict pullback, since every path in a discrete simplicial set is constant. Apply [lem-coef-equifibered-bisimplicial-diagonal] to $p$. For each $b$ the strict fiber of $p_0$ is $RN D_b$, so its canonical constant-base comparison to $\operatorname{hofib}_b(R\operatorname{diag}p)$ is a weak equivalence. All hypotheses concern rowwise Kan complexes and rowwise Kan fibrations, not fibrancy of the diagonals.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.12, printed p.183 (PDF p.198); agent-written two-sided bisimplicial resolution of its ordinary-category specialization. The equifibered diagonal input is an existing cited theorem.

proof.text: Let $A=ND_b$, $W=\operatorname{diag}Z$, and $V=\operatorname{diag}X$. Let $i_b:A\to W$ repeat $b$ and its identity base arrows, and let $j_b:RA\to V$ be the row-zero inclusion. Degreewise $d i_b=j_b u_A$, where $u$ is the characteristic-map unit. Write $F_W=\operatorname{hofib}_b(Rq)$ and $F_V=\operatorname{hofib}_b(R\operatorname{diag}p)$. Step 3 gives a weak equivalence $a_b:RA\to F_V$ whose total-space component is $u_Vj_b$ and whose path is constant. Define $k_b:RRA\to F_V$ using $Rj_b$ and constant paths. Naturality of $u$ gives $k_bu_{RA}=a_b$, so $k_b$ is a weak equivalence. Define $f_b:RA\to F_W$ using $Ri_b$ and constant paths. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] to $Rd$ over $\mathrm{id}_{RN\mathcal B}$: both total spaces and the common base are Kan, $Rd$ is a weak equivalence, and the square commutes strictly. Its induced fiber map $h_b:F_W\to F_V$ is therefore a weak equivalence. Applying $R$ to $d i_b=j_bu_A$ gives $h_bf_b=k_bR(u_A)$. The unit $u_{RA}$ and the map $R(u_A)$ are weak equivalences by Step 2. Thus the right-hand side is a weak equivalence, and cancellation with $h_b$ proves that the specified constant-path comparison $f_b$ is a weak equivalence.

proof.text: Fix $n$ and a chain $e_0\to\cdots\to e_n$. In the $m$-direction its summand of $Z$ is the nerve of $Ue_n\downarrow\mathcal B$: its chains are precisely $Ue_n\to b_0\to\cdots\to b_m$. This category has initial object $(Ue_n,1)$, and its unique arrows from that object give a natural transformation from the constant functor at it to the identity. By [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] its nerve maps weakly equivalently to a point. The augmentation $Z_{\bullet,n}\to(N\mathcal E)_n$, regarded as a discrete simplicial set, is consequently a weak equivalence on each summand and hence on their disjoint union: path components and every based homotopy group are computed inside a summand. The exchanged-direction clause of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] now proves that the particular augmentation $t:\operatorname{diag}Z\to N\mathcal E$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.12, printed p.183 (PDF p.198); agent-written two-sided bisimplicial resolution of its ordinary-category specialization. The equifibered diagonal input is an existing cited theorem.

proof.text: Write $q:\operatorname{diag}Z\to N\mathcal B$ for the base-chain projection. There is a specific simplicial homotopy $N U\,t\simeq q$. On a diagonal $n$-simplex its natural-transformation components are $Ue_i\to Ue_n\xrightarrow{\alpha}b_0\to b_i$. Commutativity follows by associativity along the two chains. To specify the entire homotopy, a monotone $\theta:[n]\to[1]$ selects $Ue_i$ when $\theta(i)=0$ and $b_i$ when $\theta(i)=1$; at the single switch use the corresponding composite $Ue_i\to b_j$. These formulas commute with every simplex operator; in particular deleting the last $e$-vertex precomposes $\alpha$ with its last $U$-arrow, which preserves each displayed component. Realize this homotopy using [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder], then apply singular complexes and the characteristic singular interval. This gives exactly a specified homotopy $RNU\,Rt\simeq Rq$. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] to $Rt$ over the identity of $RN\mathcal B$, with this homotopy. Step 5 and naturality of the units make $Rt$ a weak equivalence, so the resulting map $\operatorname{hofib}_b(Rq)\to\operatorname{hofib}_b(RNU)$ is a weak equivalence for every $b$.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.12, printed p.183 (PDF p.198); agent-written two-sided bisimplicial resolution of its ordinary-category specialization. The equifibered diagonal input is an existing cited theorem.

proof.text: Compose the comparison of Step 4 with the fiber map of Step 6. On the included comma nerve $ND_b$, all $b$-vertices and all base arrows are constant identities. The components in Step 6 reduce to $Ue_i\to Ue_n\xrightarrow{\alpha}b$, precisely the nerve of the natural transformation from $U$ of the forgetful functor to the constant functor at $b$. Denote its realized homotopy by $H_b:|ND_b|\times[0,1]\to|N\mathcal B|$. The composite comparison has the same point component as $c_{U,b}$ and follows $H_b$ before the constant endpoint path. Use equal half-intervals for this concatenation, so its path coordinate is $H_b(z,\min(2t,1))$; the path coordinate of $c_{U,b}$ is $H_b(z,t)$. The continuous formula $H_b(z,\lambda_s(t))$, where $\lambda_s(t)=\min(t/(1-s/2),1)$ for $0\leq s,t\leq1$, interpolates between them and fixes both path endpoints. It defines a simplicial cylinder homotopy on $RN D_b$: for a singular simplex $\sigma:|\Delta^n|\to|ND_b|$ and a monotone $\theta:[n]\to[1]$, substitute $z=\sigma(x)$ and $s=\sum_{\theta(i)=1}x_i$. The formula commutes with precomposition by every affine simplex operator and keeps the point component fixed. For any simplicial set $L$, the cylinder projection $L\times\Delta^1\to L$ is a simplicial homotopy equivalence: its section at zero has the homotopy $(a,s,t)\mapsto(a,\min(s,t))$ from section-composed-with-projection to the identity. By [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] the projection is a weak equivalence, so both endpoint inclusions are weak equivalences by their identity composites with it. The two endpoint maps of our comparison homotopy consequently have the same weak-equivalence status by two-out-of-three. Both factors of the composite comparison are weak equivalences, hence $c_{U,b}$ is one as well.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.12, printed p.183 (PDF p.198); agent-written two-sided bisimplicial resolution of its ordinary-category specialization. The equifibered diagonal input is an existing cited theorem.

proof.text: For a strictly commuting square $GU=U\prime F$, applying $F$ to the $e$-chain and $G$ to the $b$-chain and connecting arrow gives maps of every bisimplicial construction above. They commute with the characteristic-map units, both augmentations, and the explicit prism formula in Step 6. On the repeated-$b$ row-zero summand the map is $(e,\alpha)\mapsto(F(e),G\alpha)$, and on the target fiber it applies $RNF$ and $RNG$ to the point and path. This proves the specified naturality of $c$, rather than just existence of an abstract fiber equivalence. If $\mathcal E$ is empty, every $Z_m,X_m$ and both fiber comparisons are empty. If $\mathcal B$ is empty there is no $b$ to check. If $D_b$ is empty its inclusion and all comparisons above remain defined; Step 3 detects the empty fiber without imposing contractibility or nonemptiness.
